_comment: N-400 FORM KNOWLEDGE. What the form asks, what its terms mean in USCIS's
own published words, and what the form does NOT ask.
IT MAY NOT CONTAIN WHAT SHE SHOULD ANSWER. policy-matrix.json permits
`explain_question_literal` on the stated basis that it is 'reading back
what USCIS itself publishes about a question, in plainer words'. Every row
here carries a `source` for that reason: an uncited row is outside the
capability that authorises this file. DOJ EOIR's fraud guide: a
non-attorney 'CANNOT tell you which immigration forms to use or what
answers to put on the forms'. A row that suggests an answer is not a gap
in this file, it is a defect in it.
FAILS CLOSED. An absent row means GP does not know, and the lane must say
so rather than improvise. conf-v25 turn 104 asserted an answer about
Selective Service she never gave, using fields that exist in the catalog
but not in her record. Improvisation on a federal form is a false
statement.
NOT a placeholder: N-400's standing rule is that GP never creates empty
files for their bespoke names, because a placeholder turns a loud 404 into
a silent versioned {}.
THE FORM PRINTS ITS OWN GLOSSES for three of these, in parentheses, in
plain words already written for a lay reader. Use USCIS's words, never a
paraphrase: v25 shipped four glosses GP wrote and two of them NARROWED
the question, which changes what she is answering yes or no to.
These appear in the printed page text and ZERO times in the AcroForm
field labels, so an accessibility dump of the same PDF shows no glosses
at all and invites exactly that paraphrase.

bear_arms.source: USCIS Form N-400 (ed. 01/20/25), Part 9 Item 35, printed parenthetical
bear_arms.note: USCIS publishes no definition beyond this parenthetical. Do not add one.

noncombatant_services.gloss_official_en: do something that does not include fighting in a war
noncombatant_services.source: USCIS Form N-400 (ed. 01/20/25), Part 9 Item 36, printed parenthetical

work_of_national_importance.term_en: work of national importance under civilian direction
work_of_national_importance.gloss_official_en: do non-military work that the U.S. Government says is important to the country
work_of_national_importance.source: USCIS Form N-400 (ed. 01/20/25), Part 9 Item 37, printed parenthetical
work_of_national_importance.note: This is NOT limited to wartime or to an emergency. The form says neither.

title_of_nobility.term_en: hereditary title or an order of nobility
title_of_nobility.form_wording_en: a hereditary title or an order of nobility in any foreign country
unsettled: No official source defines whether a courtesy title, an honorific, or a
non-hereditary honour such as a knighthood counts. If she asks, say so
and name USCIS or an attorney. Do not guess on her behalf.

oath_modification._comment: The only rule here whose breach cannot be undone by a later correction.
source: USCIS Form N-400 Instructions (ed. 01/20/25): 'You may not request a modification to the portion of the Oath requiring you to perform work of national importance under civilian direction.'
12 USCIS-PM J.3(A)(1): 'There is no exemption from the clause.'
oath_modification.say: A modification exists for bearing arms and for noncombatant services, and USCIS decides it. For work of national importance there is none.
oath_modification.never_say: Any implication that the work-of-national-importance clause can be modified, waived, exempted or skipped.

_comment: Conflating these routes someone through a clear-and-convincing-evidence test they never needed.
affirmation_is_not_a_modification.say: Substituting 'solemnly affirm' for 'on oath', and omitting 'so help me God', is available on request alone, for any reason, with no evidence and no showing. That is different from a religious modification of the bearing-arms or noncombatant clauses.

_comment: THE NEGATIVE SPACE, the half nothing else in the system has. Two of the
worst defects found were the lane speaking about things the form does not
ask: a widow's deceased husband, and a Selective Service answer she never
gave.

deceased_or_former_spouse.asks: Part 5 asks a widowed or divorced applicant ONLY her marital status and how many times she has been married, then skips to Part 6.
does_not_ask: the deceased or former spouse's name
their date of birth or A-Number
the date of the marriage, the death, or the divorce
deceased_or_former_spouse.source: USCIS Form N-400 (ed. 01/20/25) Part 5. Items 4.a-8 are gated on filing under Part 1 Item 1.b or 1.d; every spouse field reads 'current spouse'.
deceased_or_former_spouse.say: The form only asks about your marital status here, so there is nothing more I need about him.
deceased_or_former_spouse.say_es: Lo siento. El formulario sólo pregunta por su estado civil aquí, así que no necesito nada más sobre él.
still_true_of_the_case: The form does not ask, but USCIS still requires EVIDENCE that prior
marriages ended, and an officer may ask at interview. 'The form does
not ask' is true of the FIELDS and false of the CASE. Say both.

children_18_and_over.asks: Part 6 asks only about children UNDER 18.
children_18_and_over.source: USCIS N-400 FAQ (2024 redesign): 'The new Form N-400 now only asks information about an applicant's children under 18.'

parents.asks: Nothing. The former Part 6 about parents was removed in the 04/01/24 edition.
parents.note: The only parent question is Part 2 Item 10, and it exists to tell her she may ALREADY be a citizen and should file N-600 instead.

good_moral_character_is_not_a_question.asks: Nothing. The word 'moral' does not appear in the form body.
good_moral_character_is_not_a_question.note: Good moral character is the STANDARD the Part 9 answers are used to assess. It is never a question she answers.

hazards._comment: Things that would send her somewhere wrong. Checked 2026-09-06.

selective_service_status_letter.hazard: The USCIS instructions still tell applicants to obtain a Selective Service Status Information Letter at www.sss.gov/verify/sil/. THAT PAGE IS A 404. SSS stopped issuing status letters on 2026-06-30 and neither USCIS document has been revised.
selective_service_status_letter.action: NEVER tell her to obtain a Status Information Letter.
selective_service_status_letter.source: Selective Service System FAQ; USCIS N-400 Instructions (ed. 01/20/25), unrevised
selective_service_status_letter.unsettled: Whether USCIS accepts any substitute is not officially established.

fee_reduction_floor.hazard: The 2024 USCIS FAQ says the reduced fee is for household income 'between 150% and 400%' of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. The CURRENT instructions and Form G-1055 both say 400% or less, with no floor.
fee_reduction_floor.action: Encode 400% or less. Never tell someone below 150% that she is ineligible.
fee_reduction_floor.source: USCIS Form N-400 Instructions (ed. 01/20/25); Form G-1055 (ed. 05/29/26)

no_fee_on_the_form.hazard: No dollar amount appears anywhere on the N-400 or its 29 pages of instructions; both delegate to Form G-1055.
no_fee_on_the_form.action: Read fees from G-1055, never from the form.
